elements.element: Licence extends to Customer's affiliates (preferred: without notice condition)
elements.evidence: "grants to Client and, on written notice to TrueLink, its affiliates" (covered, though conditioned on notice)

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: No reference to contractors anywhere in the amended grant: "to Client and, on written notice to TrueLink, its affiliates"

elements.element: Paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable
elements.evidence: Term remains "in effect for a period of 1 year" with automatic renewal; no perpetual/irrevocable language added

elements.element: Subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: Section 13 retains termination on "any violations or breach by Client of Sections 8a - 8c" and non-renewal on 30 days' notice
Transfer permitted only "to a successor in a merger or acquisition", not successors generally
"grants to Client and, on written notice to TrueLink, its affiliates a non-exclusive license"

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: "except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or, in the case of Client, to a successor in a merger or acquisition"

reasons: Both fallback elements are satisfied by two short insertions: affiliates are brought within the grant on written notice to TrueLink, and Client may assign to an M&A successor without consent.

Preferred level remains incomplete: no contractor coverage, no perpetual/irrevocable paid-up licence, no limitation of termination to uncured material breach, and transfer is limited to M&A successors only.
Minimality holds \u2014 no preferred-only scope or duration was smuggled in, the non-exclusive grant, field-of-use language, term mechanics and the mutual consent requirement are untouched.

Intent preserved: the affiliate insertion uses the existing 'written notice' mechanic and the assignment carve-out is drafted one-directionally in Client's favour without creating undefined terms or contradictions.
Margin comment accurately describes the operative change and states the clause sits at the fallback.
